clue.text: Agreeable substance

definitions.meaning: willing or satisfied, as in being happy to go along with something
what something holds or is made of, its matter or gist

explanation.surface: A pleasant material, described in two words.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: con-TENT (pleased) and CON-tent (matter).
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable the word means satisfied and willing; stressed on the first it means the material or gist inside something.

clue.text: Hackney accommodation

parts.note: read as housing in the London borough, but meant as places for hackney carriages to wait

explanation.surface: Housing in Hackney, a borough of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: A hackney carriage is the formal name for a licensed taxi; Hackney is also a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranks where licensed taxis park while waiting for fares.

clue.text: Distinguished — if incompetent

definitions.meaning: split in two it says lacking the ability

explanation.surface: A person of eminence who turns out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from splitting the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means eminent; as two words it means lacking capacity, the state of being incompetent.

clue.text: Possibly rue never turning brown

parts.note: rue is a herb that keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of a plant that never withers brown

explanation.surface: Perhaps regret that never fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like regret but is the herb; 'Possibly' marks it as one example of the kind of plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that keep green leaves through winter, never going brown, of which rue is one.

clue.text: Mark's flash!

definitions.meaning: a checkmark showing something is correct
an instant, as in 'back in a flash'

explanation.surface: Mark is quick!
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a check sign on a list and a moment of time, as in 'just a second'.

clue.text: A piece for the odd recital

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of recital are set in a peculiar new order

explanation.surface: A short composition suitable for an unusual concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges the letters of RECITAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper article is a piece of writing, so the two words are synonyms in journalism.

clue.text: Warning donor it may need alteration

indicators.note: need alteration says the letters of donor it may must be changed around

explanation.surface: Telling a donor that their gift may have to be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need alteration' rearranges DONOR IT MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautionary or reproving, giving a caution to someone.

clue.text: Two of which are proverbially disagreeable?

definitions.text: Two of which are proverbially disagreeable?

parts.words: Two of which are proverbially disagreeable?
parts.note: from the proverb that two of a kind in the same line of business never agree

explanation.surface: A pair that, according to the proverb, never get on.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'two of a trade never agree' says rivals in one business always quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of business or craft; the proverb says two practitioners of it will quarrel.

clue.text: Outsider put over state body

indicators.note: put over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a cad is an ill-bred man, an outsider in the old British slang sense
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: An outsider takes charge of a state body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outsider' is old British slang for a bounder. 'State body' looks like a government agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body, especially one for dissection.

clue.text: Record among the Top Ten Roll out the Barrel

indicators.note: among tells us the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

parts.words: the Top Ten Roll out the Barrel

explanation.surface: A popular old song, 'Roll Out the Barrel', makes the top ten of the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'Ten Roll'. 'Record' looks like a chart disc but means to register.
explanation.definitionFit: To register a name on an official list, as when signing up for a course.

clue.text: The graduate first to get into the swim

indicators.note: first tells us the graduate's letters come before the other word

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate's degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new graduate is the first to plunge into the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' places BA ahead of THE. 'Get into the swim' usually means joining in socially; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to go for a swim, literally getting into the water.

clue.text: Officer giving Jack his orders?

parts.note: Jack Tar is a sailor, so the officer is a naval one of high rank directing the crew

explanation.surface: An officer barking instructions at a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack Tar, is an old name for a sailor; the naval rank between captain and lieutenant commander fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval officer of senior rank issues orders to the seamen under them.

clue.text: Island to visit to shoot duck?

parts.note: taken as written
to bag game is to shoot and take it
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A holiday island where one might go wildfowling.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O. 'Duck' looks like the bird to be shot, but it is only the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island paired with Trinidad, a place a holidaymaker might go.

clue.text: Break travel in a different way

indicators.note: in a different way tells us the letters of travel in are put into another order

explanation.surface: Interrupting a journey by taking an alternative route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different way' rearranges TRAVEL IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause or rest between parts, as at a theatre.

clue.text: Exceptionally noble, so apt to be a server

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually aristocratic person suited to waiting at table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally' rearranges NOBLE SO APT. The 'server' is a large serving spoon, not a waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spoon used for serving food at table.

clue.text: A relative will be critical about one point

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the compass letter

parts.note: nice can mean precise or finely discriminating, as in a nice distinction
E, East, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A family member is going to be scathing about a single detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critical' here is the old sense of nice: exacting and finely judged, not kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Aircraft circling round overhead (with their self-banking systems?)

parts.note: auto- is the Greek-derived prefix meaning self
giro is a bank transfer system, as in the old National Giro

explanation.surface: Helicopter-like craft circling above, supposedly equipped with their own bank services.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro is a system of credit transfers between banks, familiar in Britain from the Post Office's Girobank. 'Self-banking' also hints at an aircraft banking itself as it turns.
explanation.definitionFit: An early rotor aircraft whose overhead blades spin freely to give lift.

clue.text: An old fighter — cheerful one surmounting a height

indicators.note: in a down clue surmounting means the earlier pieces sit on top of the next

parts.note: glad means happy or cheerful
I is the Roman numeral one
a tor is a rocky hill or height, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter is happy to climb a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky peak, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena combatant who fought for public entertainment.

clue.text: A fool will go easy on the heavyweight

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece is placed on top of the next

parts.note: simple means easy
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: An idiot will go gently on the big boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go easy on' looks like a phrase meaning be lenient; here 'on' just stacks one piece above another.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish, gullible person is a dimwit.

clue.text: Very little drops from this

parts.note: read as tiny droplets falling from a garden device, not as hardly anything falling

explanation.surface: Something from which almost nothing falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little drops' reads as 'hardly anything falls' but means 'very small droplets', as from a lawn watering device.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden watering device scatters water in fine droplets.

clue.text: Work out or break down

definitions.meaning: to solve a problem or settle a matter
to separate into component parts, as a chemist does

explanation.surface: Solve a puzzle or collapse in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to settle or solve something and to separate it into its constituents.

clue.text: A pound the Greek character returns the book!

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

indicators.note: returns means the Greek letter's name is written backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a pound and a Greek person gives back a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MU into UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank book for photographs or stamps is called by this name.

clue.text: Ask for directions in a wood

indicators.note: in tells us the directions go inside the tree's name

parts.note: beech is a wood used in furniture
S and E are the compass directions south and east

explanation.surface: Asking for the way while lost in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directions' suggests route-finding but means two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or implore someone earnestly for something.

clue.text: Make known, underworld boss secure

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god ruling the underworld
to close something is to secure it shut

explanation.surface: Revealing that a gangland chief is safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, ruler of the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or divulge information is to let it be known.

clue.text: The Cockney's wife is not British

definitions.meaning: 'my old ...' is Cockney slang for one's wife
from the Netherlands rather than Britain

explanation.surface: A Londoner's wife turns out to be foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner; 'my old Dutch' is their phrase for a wife, from an old music-hall song.
explanation.definitionFit: Londoners of the East End call a wife 'my old Dutch'; the word also describes people of the Netherlands, who are foreign rather than British.

clue.text: Catch a girl out initially

parts.note: lass is a girl

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word out

explanation.surface: Spotting a girl going out at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' looks like a verb about spotting someone, but it is the rope used to catch cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose used to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: Gaudy stuff can almost find a buyer.

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to sell is to find a buyer for goods

explanation.surface: Cheap glitter that is hard to get rid of in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last L of SELL, leaving SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittery strips used as cheap showy decoration at Christmas.

clue.text: A place likely to be blown up

definitions.text: A place likely to be blown up

parts.words: A place likely to be blown up
parts.note: sounds like a target for explosives, but the fire on a funeral heap is fanned into flame

explanation.surface: A site likely to be destroyed by explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests an explosion, but here it means a fire fanned into blaze on a heap for burning a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of wood on which a corpse is burned, whose flames the wind fans.

clue.text: Embroidered yarn

parts.note: read as decorated thread, but meant as an exaggerated tale

explanation.surface: Thread used in needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embroidered' means exaggerated and 'yarn' means a tale, not sewing thread.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, hard-to-believe tale is one that has been embellished.

clue.text: The sober man imbibes little, so is sound as a bird

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so the abstainer's letters take another word inside them

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes a man who drinks no alcohol
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A teetotaller sips only a drop and so stays in perfect health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like healthy, as in 'sound as a bell', but it is a noise. TT stands for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bird's chirp is its call or song.

clue.text: New hood specially designed for an American festivity

indicators.note: specially designed means the letters of new hood are reshaped into a fresh form

explanation.surface: A new bonnet made to order for a party in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially designed' rearranges NEW HOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: An American country-dance party, a lively social gathering with square dancing.

clue.text: A hearing device at that time made from clay

parts.note: the ear is the organ we hear with
then means at that time

explanation.surface: An old ear trumpet fashioned from clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing device' suggests a hearing aid, but it is simply the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery fired from baked soil is described with this adjective.
